Let's review some fundamental engineering terminology that you'll encounter throughout your studies.
Understanding these terms will provide a solid foundation for your engineering education.

rows.text: The practice of using natural science, mathematics and the design process to solve technical problems and improve systems
A creative, inventive person who finds solutions to practical problems (from Latin ingenium/ingeniare)
One of the oldest disciplines; from civilian engineers — the first non-military engineers
The oldest form of engineering: fortifications, siege works, roads for armies
Design disciplined by analysis: physics, materials, cost, manufacturability, safety

narr: Let's start with some core engineering terms.
Engineering refers to the practice of applying scientific and mathematical principles to solve practical problems.
An engineer is a creative professional who develops solutions to technical challenges.
Civil engineering is one of the oldest engineering disciplines, focusing on infrastructure and public works.
Military engineering predates civil engineering and involves fortifications and military infrastructure.
Engineering design is a systematic process that considers physics, materials, cost, and safety.

rows.text: A discipline's organization: standards, continuing education, a code of ethics (ASME, IEEE, ASCE, AIChE, AIAA, ANS)
A body of rules ensuring that the profession serves the interests of society, the employer, the profession and oneself
A rule of acceptable conduct for a particular group (historically, church laws)
Standards of behavior by which people judge the morality of personal and group situations

narr: Now let's explore terms related to professional practice in engineering.
A professional society is an organization that establishes standards, provides continuing education, and maintains a code of ethics for a specific engineering discipline.
A code of ethics is a set of rules that ensures engineers serve society, their employers, the profession, and themselves with integrity.
A canon refers to a rule of acceptable conduct for a particular group, historically associated with church laws.
Personal ethics are the standards of behavior that people use to judge the morality of their own actions and those of others.
